chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I said, 'The one in Ihram is pestered by flies when he intends to sleep; can he cover his face?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, but he should not cover his head; and the woman, when sleeping, there is no harm if she covers her entire face when sleeping.'

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: Can a person in Ihram cover their face from flies while sleeping?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi through the chain of Zurarah, a key companion of Imam al-Baqir, this hadith clarifies the distinction between covering the head (prohibited for men) and the face (permitted for protection). It highlights the practical jurisprudence of Ihram, noting that while men must keep their heads exposed to remain in a state of ritual readiness, women are granted flexibility to cover their faces entirely during sleep, reflecting the specific conditions of the sacred state.
